## Request

New real PM items should use the autogenerated ID. Agents should put descriptive names in the title and retain GitHub issue numbers as external references, rather than assigning names such as `pm-preview-path-refusal` as item identity.

Make identity policy configurable through project settings, with autogenerated IDs as the ordinary default and explicit overrides available when deliberately enabled. Avoid static hardcoded guards or title/name heuristics.

Please make this the ordinary agent workflow and evaluate a safe, audited migration for existing real items whose IDs were manually assigned. This issue requests design and implementation work; it does not authorize an immediate bulk rewrite of the current tracker.

## Verified current behavior

Autogeneration is already the runtime default. At main `4c1e4e3cb9f6e40411261ade638297e69ee65d5e`:

- [`resolveCreateItemId`](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/blob/4c1e4e3cb9f6e40411261ade638297e69ee65d5e/src/sdk/lifecycle/create.ts#L1679-L1709) calls `generateItemId` only when the explicit ID is undefined
- A supplied `id` / `--id` bypasses generation and is normalized and validated as letters, numbers and dashes
- [The generator](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/blob/4c1e4e3cb9f6e40411261ade638297e69ee65d5e/src/core/item/id.ts) produces the configured prefix plus a random base36 token, with configured token length and collision handling

The gap is ordinary task-creation practice and its guidance/policy boundary: agents can use the explicit-ID escape hatch for names instead of consuming the generated identity. This is not a claim that the default generator derives IDs from titles or has stopped working.

## Confirmed production examples

1. [`pm-preview-path-refusal`](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/blob/4c1e4e3cb9f6e40411261ade638297e69ee65d5e/.agents/pm/issues/pm-preview-path-refusal.toon) is a real closed Issue, not a fixture. Its [creation history](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/blob/4c1e4e3cb9f6e40411261ade638297e69ee65d5e/.agents/pm/history/pm-preview-path-refusal.jsonl) records this exact ID at 2026-10-07T05:16:46.951Z, author `harness:codex`, during the merge-recovery/preview-refusal implementation.
2. [`pm-ledger-sparse-delivery`](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/blob/4c1e4e3cb9f6e40411261ade638297e69ee65d5e/.agents/pm/changesets/pm-ledger-sparse-delivery.toon) is a real Changeset for the #1438 sparse-array repair. Its [creation history](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/blob/4c1e4e3cb9f6e40411261ade638297e69ee65d5e/.agents/pm/history/pm-ledger-sparse-delivery.jsonl) records creation at 2026-10-11T07:38:34.006Z by `harness:codex`. The original report retained the existing generated owner `pm-q91qyd`; the later implementation added this named Changeset.

A bounded tree inventory at that revision found 2,928 item `.toon` paths, including 24 visibly descriptive multi-hyphen names and 50 `pm-gh<number>` names. These are filename-pattern counts only, not proof that all those items require migration. The two examples above were checked against their actual metadata and creation history. Random-looking IDs can also have been explicitly supplied; shape alone is not provenance.

## Proposed behavior

- Ordinary new real items leave `id` unset across CLI, SDK, MCP and agent examples. Capture the committed generated ID from the create receipt and use it for subsequent references; do not predict it from a title or repeat creation after an uncertain acknowledgement.
- Define a validated, discoverable ID-policy setting through the existing configuration/schema primitives, with autogenerated IDs as the ordinary default. Explicit IDs remain available when deliberately enabled for the relevant workflow. Use the same effective policy in CLI, SDK, MCP and extension-backed creation; do not implement static hardcoded guards, special cases for particular names, or per-harness rules.
- Document configuration scope and precedence, effective-policy inspection, configuration discovery, and actionable recovery when an explicit override is disabled. Reject invalid policy values consistently. Any exact setting names or enum values are design proposals until implemented; reuse existing settings validation and extension contracts rather than introducing parallel configuration machinery.
- Preserve intentional import/source-identity preservation, isolated deterministic fixtures and documented content-addressed/idempotent integration identities. These are explicit exceptions to ordinary task creation, not blanket reasons to manually name new work items.
- Record enough creation provenance to distinguish generated identity from an intentional override going forward. Do not fabricate provenance for old items.
- Keep existing consumers compatible through an explicit policy/version transition. Do not silently remove useful SDK primitives.

## Evaluate selective migration, with history intact

Reuse/extend the existing migration owner [`pm-kl19`](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/blob/4c1e4e3cb9f6e40411261ade638297e69ee65d5e/.agents/pm/issues/pm-kl19.toon) and schema-evolution machinery. Its prefix-migration work already owns typed plan/apply/verify, reference consistency, history integrity and crash-safe auditing. Selective regeneration of confirmed manually assigned IDs is an additional use case, not a competing migration subsystem.

Required boundaries before any apply:

1. Inventory candidates using creation provenance and explicit review, not ID-shape heuristics. Report unknown provenance, intentional imported identities and fixture exclusions separately.
2. Provide a non-mutating dry run with the complete selected old-to-new mapping, generated-ID reservation/collision checks, affected items, references and verification plan. A reviewed plan must retain its mapping on retry.
3. Account for every inbound and outbound reference: parents, dependencies/blockers, plan links, schema/extension-owned ID fields, focus/claims, receipts, cursors, indexes, documents and cross-workspace or external links. Identify unsupported reference types and refuse incomplete apply rather than silently leaving stale links.
4. Preserve immutable historical evidence and its hash chains. Specify how historical IDs, as-of reads, old links and aliases/redirects resolve through a durable audited identity mapping; never rewrite old JSONL history merely to make hashes fit.
5. Provide verified backups, locked transactional/resumable application, crash recovery, idempotent retries and audited rollback that preserves later valid work. Keep old IDs reserved and define collision/alias-cycle behavior.
6. Verify graph/reference consistency, current state, retained history and old/new addressing after apply. External systems that cannot be updated atomically need durable compatibility mappings and explicit unresolved-reference reporting.
7. Never implement this as filename-only renaming, direct global search/replace, delete-and-recreate without lineage, or automatic regeneration of every descriptive-looking ID.

## Acceptance and regression coverage

- Normal CLI/SDK/MCP creation returns an autogenerated ID and adequate receipt; subsequent relationships use that returned ID. Cover custom types and configured prefixes/token lengths.
- Ordinary agent guidance and examples do not teach named IDs for new real tasks. Verify the default generated-ID policy, deliberately enabled explicit overrides, invalid settings, scope/precedence and effective-policy discovery through consistent CLI/SDK/MCP and extension paths.
- Policy changes are configuration-driven, not static guards; refused creates preserve authoritative bytes and provide discoverable configuration/recovery guidance. Override provenance and compatibility transitions remain explicit.
- Import preservation, deterministic fixtures and deliberate content-addressed integrations retain their documented contracts under explicit exceptions.
- Candidate inventory correctly separates proven overrides, generated IDs and unknown provenance, including a manually supplied random-looking ID and an intentional descriptive imported ID.
- Migration dry run changes no authoritative bytes; apply preserves item content, all registered references, immutable history and historical reads.
- Regression tests cover duplicate/colliding destinations, alias collisions/cycles, unmappable external or extension references, concurrent writes, partial failure, resume, repeated apply, verified backup/restore and rollback.
- Existing named production records stay usable until a reviewed migration is actually applied. New work recorded for this issue should itself use an autogenerated item ID.

## Related ownership and duplicate check

All-status searches covered explicit IDs, generated IDs, named IDs, manual IDs, autogeneration, override behavior and ID rename/migration.

- #548 is a closed GitHub mirror; its comments explicitly retain open canonical [`pm-kl19`](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/blob/4c1e4e3cb9f6e40411261ade638297e69ee65d5e/.agents/pm/issues/pm-kl19.toon). Reuse that migration foundation.
- #600 / [`pm-pibw`](https://github.com/unbraind/pm-cli/blob/4c1e4e3cb9f6e40411261ade638297e69ee65d5e/.agents/pm/issues/pm-pibw.toon) cover collision-resistant generation, not ordinary override policy.
- #860 covers imported source-ID fidelity, #786 deterministic/reproducible fixtures, and #1400 typed duplicate-ID conflicts for deliberate content-addressed callers. Preserve those use cases.

No exact existing ordinary-create guardrail issue was found in this focused check. No implementation or tracker migration was performed for this report.
Configure generated identity defaults and explicit override policy across SDK transports

Implement GitHub issue1442 through discoverable project configuration and shared SDK creation policy. Ordinary new work consumes the generated create receipt; deliberate import and integration identities remain explicit. Evaluate selective migration through pm-kl19 without applying any real tracker migration.

Configuration-driven effective identity policy is consistent across CLI SDK MCP and extensions; default creates return generated IDs and preserved receipt identities; intentional override/import behavior has explicit compatibility and provenance; invalid settings and refused overrides preserve bytes and have recovery; migration is dry-run-first and preserves historical identities through the canonical migration owner.
Ordinary work uses generated identities while deliberate overrides remain governed and discoverable, and migration preserves recorded history and references.
